name: ai-sre-incidents
description: Incident scenarios with ground truth for the AI SRE investigator. Faults use the simulator's fault types; worlds are generated deterministically from them (evals/src/ai_sre_evals/world.py).

scenarios.title: Orders deploy introduces an N+1 query and saturates the DB pool
scenarios.description: orders-service 2.4.0 adds line items to the order-history endpoint with one query per item. Pool waits and timeouts follow; the gateway passes the 503s on. An unrelated gateway release went out 4 minutes earlier.
scenarios.query: Why has API latency increased and why are orders failing in the last 15 minutes?

deployments.changes_summary: Checkout banner copy update; bump httpx to 0.28.1
deployments.author: a.rahman

deployments.changes_summary: Order history: include line items for each order (mobile app v5)
deployments.author: m.okafor

scenarios.title: Redis becomes unreachable
scenarios.description: The Redis host black-holes traffic. Carts fail, catalog reads fall back to the database, orders are charged but cannot be queued for fulfilment. No deployment in the window.
scenarios.query: Carts are returning errors and some orders are failing, what is going on?

scenarios.title: Upstream payments provider returns errors
scenarios.description: The third-party payments provider fails about half of the charge calls with 503. Order placement fails; nothing changed on our side.
scenarios.query: Customers report checkout failures when placing orders

scenarios.title: Network latency on the path to PostgreSQL
scenarios.description: A degraded network path adds ~120 ms to every round trip to the database. Every DB-backed endpoint on every service slows down in proportion to its query count while the database itself is idle.
scenarios.query: Everything feels slow: API latency is up across the shop for the last 20 minutes

scenarios.title: Feature flag leaks DB connections until the pool is exhausted
scenarios.description: A config change enables the audit-trail flag on orders-service; a code path leaves transactions open, connections sit idle in transaction and the pool runs dry.
scenarios.query: orders-service is timing out and orders are failing

scenarios.title: Failed api-gateway canary keeps serving traffic
scenarios.description: api-gateway 3.9.0 rejects a configuration value; the canary fails health checks and the deploy is marked failed, but the broken canary replicas (25%) were never scaled down.
scenarios.query: About a quarter of API requests are failing with 500s

deployments.author: a.rahman
deployments.failure_reason: canary failed health checks (25% of replicas)

scenarios.title: api-gateway deploy adds an unbounded cache (memory leak)
scenarios.description: api-gateway 3.10.0 adds an in-process response cache without a bound. Memory grows until the container is OOM-killed; the gateway restarts every few minutes and latency spikes.
scenarios.query: api-gateway keeps restarting and latency spikes every few minutes

deployments.changes_summary: Add in-process response cache for catalog
deployments.author: j.lee

scenarios.title: Worker deploy breaks shipping labels; the queue backs up
scenarios.description: fulfilment-worker 1.7.0 switches to a new label API client that times out; jobs fail and retry, and the fulfilment queue grows. The API looks healthy.
scenarios.query: Orders are not being fulfilled; the fulfilment queue keeps growing

deployments.changes_summary: Shipping labels: switch to v2 label API client
deployments.author: r.diaz

scenarios.title: Shipping-label provider slowness backs up the queue
scenarios.description: The external shipping-label service is slow; a fraction of jobs time out. No deployment; the worker simply cannot keep up.
scenarios.query: The fulfilment queue is backing up

scenarios.title: Traffic surge beyond capacity
scenarios.description: A marketing push triples traffic. Latency rises on the gateway and orders-service; nothing is broken, the services are under-provisioned.
scenarios.query: Latency is up on the API, is something broken?

scenarios.title: Query-plan regression without a deployment
scenarios.description: An index on order_items was dropped by a manual DBA change (not in the deployment log). Order lookups become sequential scans; the orders pool saturates.
scenarios.query: Checkout is slow and some orders time out

scenarios.title: N+1 deploy while logs and database telemetry are unavailable
scenarios.description: Same failure as S01, but Loki and the database monitoring endpoints are down: only metrics, deployments, infrastructure and the knowledge base answer.
scenarios.query: Orders API is slow and failing since about 10 minutes ago

deployments.changes_summary: Order history: include line items for each order
deployments.author: m.okafor

scenarios.title: Redis outage while infrastructure monitoring is down
scenarios.description: Redis is unreachable, and the infrastructure/dependency monitoring and anomaly detector are also down. Only logs and per-service metrics remain.
scenarios.query: Carts and checkout are failing for many users

scenarios.title: Payments provider failure, orders deploy shipped after the onset
scenarios.description: Payments started failing 12 minutes ago; an orders-service release went out 6 minutes ago, after the errors began. The deploy is innocent: symptoms predate it and do not change at the deploy.
scenarios.query: Order placement has been failing for a while and we deployed orders-service a few minutes ago; was it the deploy?

deployments.changes_summary: Fix rounding of order totals for multi-quantity lines
deployments.author: s.ito

scenarios.title: Gateway errors after a gateway release, caused by an orders config change
scenarios.description: api-gateway shipped at 13 min; orders-service enabled a leaking feature flag at 12 min. Gateway 5xx are pass-through from orders-service pool exhaustion.
scenarios.query: api-gateway error rate jumped right after today's gateway release

scenarios.title: Redis slowness and payments errors at the same time
scenarios.description: Two independent failures: Redis latency (carts slow, some cache errors) from 9 min, and payments-provider errors from 7 min.
scenarios.query: Checkout is failing and carts are slow

scenarios.title: Gateway memory leak deploy plus an unrelated worker backlog
scenarios.description: api-gateway 3.10.0 leaks memory (restarts) and, independently, the label provider slows the worker.
scenarios.query: api-gateway keeps restarting and fulfilment is lagging behind

deployments.changes_summary: Add in-process response cache for catalog
deployments.author: j.lee

scenarios.title: Vague slowness report with nothing wrong
scenarios.description: A user reports the site feels slow. Latency p99 moved within normal variance; a handful of transient errors; no deployment, all dependencies healthy. The right answer is that no root cause is identifiable.
scenarios.query: Users say the site feels a bit slow today

scenarios.title: Question blames a deploy that changed nothing
scenarios.description: orders-service 2.3.2 (an email-template typo fix) shipped 20 minutes ago. A few errors happened before it. No signal changed; the deploy did not break anything.
scenarios.query: Did the 2.3.2 orders-service deploy break anything?

deployments.changes_summary: Fix typo in order confirmation email template
deployments.author: p.nair

scenarios.title: Database network latency with a misleading worker config change
scenarios.description: Network latency to PostgreSQL slows every service. A fulfilment-worker config change (log level) and an old rollback are in the deployment log.
scenarios.query: API and order processing have been slow for the last 20 minutes

deployments.changes_summary: Raise log level to DEBUG for label client
deployments.author: ci-bot

scenarios.title: Redis outage one minute after an unrelated gateway release
scenarios.description: api-gateway 3.8.1 (copy change) finished at 9 min; Redis became unreachable at 8 min. The timing points at the deploy, but orders-service and the worker fail the same way and Redis is down.
scenarios.query: Errors everywhere right after the gateway release, should we roll it back?

scenarios.title: Payments provider completely down
scenarios.description: The payments provider refuses connections. No order can be placed.
scenarios.query: Nobody can place orders right now, checkout is completely down

scenarios.title: N+1 deploy while metrics and logs backends are flaky
scenarios.description: Same failure as S01; the anomaly detector and the log aggregation time out once before answering (exercises retries).
scenarios.query: Order history endpoint is very slow since the last release

deployments.changes_summary: Order history: include line items for each order
deployments.author: m.okafor

scenarios.title: orders-service returns 500s after a release (no resource symptom)
scenarios.description: orders-service 2.5.0 has a bug in a serializer; 10% of requests fail with 500. No pool, queue or memory symptom; only the error rate and the deploy correlate.
scenarios.query: orders-service started returning 500s about ten minutes ago

scenarios.title: Redis slow (not down): catalog and carts slower
scenarios.description: Redis answers slowly (800 ms); a fraction of commands time out. Catalog falls back to the database; carts are slow and occasionally fail.
scenarios.query: Catalog pages got slower in the last 15 minutes
